usage: This is the standard and most natural way to ask if someone speaks English in Morocco. It is universally understood and works in both casual and formal contexts. While 'l-ngliziyya' is the Arabic-derived term, many Moroccans also casually say 'longli' (from French 'l'anglais').

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Use this when addressing a female, adding the feminine 'i' suffix to the verb.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Use this when addressing two or more people.

variants.label: casual alternative
variants.note: Uses the alternative verb 'dwa' (to speak) and the French-derived word for English, very common in casual street Darija.

variants.label: more polite
variants.note: Uses the verb 'to know' and adds 'please', ideal for approaching strangers like shopkeepers or police.

examples.arabic: سمح ليا اخويا، واش كتهضر النڭليزية؟
examples.transliteration: sme7 liya a khouya, wash katheder l-ngliziyya?
examples.english: Excuse me brother, do you speak English?

examples.arabic: ما كنهضرش العربية، واش كتهضري النڭليزية؟
examples.transliteration: ma kanhdersh l-3erbiyya, wash kathedri l-ngliziyya?
examples.english: I don't speak Arabic, do you (f) speak English?
Do you (pl) speak English or French?
